name: Neo
text: The bazaar stirs at dawn with no doors shuttered overnight and the graveyard empty—no Family hand has acted yet. I note Morpheus asked Sherlock the same, so to the point: which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today?

name: Neo
text: Elsa, your question to Batman asked which action by a power role tonight he would watch most closely. Name the power role and the exact action you expect, then tell us why that action matters more than the Doctor’s protection or the Detective’s investigation.

name: Neo
text:
Elsa, you asked Batman which power role to watch tonight, yet the Compact is explicit: the Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. Hermione, Yoda, Ripley and Sherlock all pressed him to cite the clause that bends that rule; he has not. Batman now re-asks for the Compact line he still cannot produce.

Sherlock, your silence on six identical questions stands out. State plainly: which merchant on the roster has not yet spoken today?

name: Neo
text: Neo: Morpheus, your insistence on naming every merchant who has spoken does not answer Sherlock’s roster question—it merely echoes the roster itself. Sherlock, state which merchant on the roster you still consider silent, or clarify what you meant by “not yet spoken.” Elsa, your latest question to Batman repeats the pattern Gandalf noted earlier—no new fact, only the same demand for a clause that none can produce. Ripley asked Batman to ground his forecast in the Compact or Herald; silence in response is evidence of its absence. Batman has now been asked seven times for the clause that bends the Compact’s plain wording. Produce it or withdraw the claim.

name: Neo
text: If Batman is honest, his vote tonight will cite the Compact clause he claims exists or retract the forecast that the Detective acts before tonight’s vote—watch whether it does.

name: Neo
text: Elsa, your eight demands for a clause that does not exist stand in the public record; the Compact’s Doctor and Detective duties follow the vote, and the roster lists every merchant’s voice today—no silence to hide behind. Morpheus, your insistence on counting spoken names does not answer Sherlock’s roster question; it merely echoes the roster itself. Sherlock, with the roster now proven complete, state plainly: which merchant on the roster did you mean to call silent, or clarify what you meant by “not yet spoken.”

name: Neo
text:
Gandalf, your citation of Compact clause 5 settles the rule—Doctor’s and Detective’s duties follow the vote, not precede it. Sherlock clarified his “silent merchant” question stayed inside the Morning region’s custom, so the roster stands complete with ten voices.

Elsa, you pressed nine times for a clause that none can produce, then named Batman despite owning the same flawed forecast—your vote test failed its only check. That leaves one merchant untouched by the ledger’s clarity: Sherlock.

Sherlock, your silence on six identical roster questions is louder than your words. Name the merchant you meant to call silent, or drop the label.

name: Neo
text:
Neo: Gandalf, Sherlock, Ripley, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Inigo—you have now all settled the roster is complete and clause 5 bars pre-vote power-role action. Elsa’s own test failed her, yet she named Batman in her vote rationale.

Batman, you have been asked nine times for the clause you claim exists and produced none. Your ninth silence still stands.

Sherlock, your regional question is answered, yet you remain silent on why your earlier phrasing mattered at all.

Yoda, Morpheus, Ripley—you have each noted the absence of provable evidence against Batman’s claim.

The bazaar’s Compact is plain; plain answers alone remain.

name: Neo
text:
Gandalf, Sherlock, Ripley, Hermione, Yoda, Morpheus, Inigo—you have now all settled the roster is complete and clause 5 bars pre-vote power-role action. Elsa named Batman in her vote rationale despite her own vote test failing her flawed forecast.

Batman, you have been asked nine times for the clause you claim exists and produced none. Your ninth silence still stands.

I lean toward banishing Elsa tonight because her vote test failed her own flawed forecast and she named the wrong merchant despite the ledger’s clarity.
